t: Definition and Terminology Resolver: a plain-language overview
title: Definition and Terminology Resolver: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Definition and Terminology Resolver does and why archives need it. A definition and terminology resolver figures out which meaning of a word you mean. 'Kernel' is a seed to a farmer, an OS core to a programmer, and a function to a statistician — the resolver reads the surrounding text, checks the field, and picks the right definition. Every term gets the meaning its context intended.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Definition and Terminology Resolver works
title: How the Definition and Terminology Resolver works
description: Overview: what the Definition and Terminology Resolver does and why archives need it. Real resolvers harvest definitions with patterns ('X is defined as...', 'X refers to...', glossary entries) and store them per domain, then disambiguate with Lesk-style algorithms: the dictionary definitions of each candidate sense are compared by word overlap against the term's surrounding context, and the best-overlapping sense wins. Domain priors weight the field's usual meaning, and technical glossaries outrank general dictionaries for specialist text. Each resolution carries the winning sense, its definition, and the overlap evidence.

t: How the Definition and Terminology Resolver works: the deep tour
title: How the Definition and Terminology Resolver works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Definition and Terminology Resolver does and why archives need it. Real resolvers harvest definitions with patterns ('X is defined as...', 'X refers to...', glossary entries) and store them per domain, then disambiguate with Lesk-style algorithms: the dictionary definitions of each candidate sense are compared by word overlap against the term's surrounding context, and the best-overlapping sense wins. Domain priors weight the field's usual meaning, and technical glossaries outrank general dictionaries for specialist text. Each resolution carries the winning sense, its definition, and the overlap evidence. Advanced systems use embedding-based similarity instead of raw word overlap, track how term meanings drift over time (a 'computer' in 1940 is a person), and handle multi-word terms whose meaning is not compositional ('hot dog'). Quality is measured by sense-accuracy on annotated corpora like SemCor. The limits are genuinely novel usages and puns that intend two meanings at once — those are reported as ambiguous with both senses rather than forced into one.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
